title: MOSFET: Enhancement vs Depletion Explained Simply | PUC Electronics
description:
Aarav's phone has a chip with billions of tiny switches, and the control gate of each one does not even touch the part it controls. That switch is a MOSFET. We start with a magnet under a glass table (it lines up iron dust without touching it), then build an n channel enhancement MOSFET: p type substrate, n type source and drain, a thin silicon dioxide layer and a metal gate. Metal, oxide, semiconductor.

On a live breadboard the gate voltage rises from 0 V: nothing happens until the threshold voltage V_T, then the gate pulls electrons under the oxide into an induced channel, the lamp lights and the oscilloscope shows the drain current rising. Then the depletion MOSFET with its built-in channel: a negative gate thins it (depletion mode), a positive gate thickens it (enhancement mode). We compare the transfer curves and the symbols (broken line vs solid line), write I_D = k(V_GS - V_T)^2 and Shockley's equation, work an example, and finish with the exam trap (an enhancement MOSFET is off at zero gate volts), where it is asked, an original practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 64 of PUC Electronics, Class 12, Chapter 1: Field Effect Transistor (FET) (Karnataka II PUC Electronics). The FET is not in the rationalised NCERT/CBSE Class 12 Physics book or the ISC Physics syllabus, so this lesson follows the Karnataka PUC Electronics syllabus.
